problem.text: The default Rich input path did not consult the multiline flag, and response presentation had no separate handling for <think> reasoning.

reasoning.text: The change unifies input through prompt_toolkit while retaining separate basic and Markdown output paths. Reasoning mode appends <think> to the formatted prompt and delays Markdown rendering until </think> appears.

impact.text: requirements_examples.txt adds prompt_toolkit, matching the new unconditional imports in chat.py. The whole-parent search found no existing literal prompt_toolkit references; it does not exclude dynamic imports or external users.
The parser now declares --multiline instead of --mli, retaining -mli. Both output modes use prompt_toolkit input, so basic mode no longer selects the old stdin reader.

source_notes.text: The earlier Markdown entry records the default input path ignoring --mli.
That active-path omission is removed: both branches now select read_input_ptk, which passes args.multiline to prompt(). The old readers remain defined but are no longer selected by main.
Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” reports native-extension loading failure and an environment workaround, not multiline input or reasoning presentation.

limitations: No interactive terminal, prompt_toolkit key bindings, Rich rendering or model inference was executed. Alt+Enter submission is advertised by the parser but not independently verified.
The bounded Python check models string routing only; it does not execute Streamer_rich or establish which chunk boundaries a model will produce.

chapters.title: Multiline input and simple reasoning presentation

claims.text: read_input_ptk wraps the colored user label in ANSI and forwards the store_true multiline option, which defaults to false. This replaces both the stdin-based reader and Prompt.ask in main's dispatch.

get_input_ids appends <think> after template formatting and before tokenization, including when context is re-tokenized during trimming. This is prompt conditioning, not a change to sampling or the model.

With --think, Streamer_rich initially prints a magenta Thinking label and accumulates flushed plain text in think_text. It searches that accumulated string for </think>, allowing detection across chunks, then starts Live. Subsequent chunks populate all_text and the Markdown display; history stores all_text.strip(), excluding the thinking buffer.

Without --think, Rich begins immediately as before. Live retains a default refresh limit of 25 updates per second, not a token-generation limit. Basic output does not implement the reasoning split: it prints and retains every generated chunk even when the prompt receives <think>.

The implementation favors a small delimiter-driven presentation state machine over structured reasoning parsing. It requires a closing delimiter to enter answer rendering and treats the entire delimiter-containing chunk as thinking.

A scalar transcription retained Answer when it arrived after a delimiter-only chunk, but produced empty history when Answer shared the closing-delimiter chunk, including when the delimiter itself spanned chunks. A stream without a closing delimiter also left history empty.

findings.description: Answer text sharing the closing-reasoning chunk is omitted from answer history.
findings.trigger: Use Rich output with --think and receive a chunk containing </think> followed by answer text.
findings.expected_behavior: Text after the closing delimiter enters the Markdown answer and saved conversation response.
findings.actual_behavior: stream prints and stores the entire chunk in think_text, then begins Live without transferring its suffix. Only later chunks enter all_text, which main uses for history.

verification.description: The whole-parent .stream( search identifies main's s.stream(chunk) as the chatbot call site. Main supplies generator result text and saves s.all_text.strip(); the diff selects Streamer_rich only outside basic mode.
verification.limits: Literal call-site search does not establish external or dynamically dispatched callers.

verification.description: Modeled the inspected accumulation and delimiter transition with separate and combined delimiter/answer chunks; combined chunks lost Answer from history.
verification.limits: Standard-library string model only; no repository streamer, terminal or generator execution.

annotation.summary: Adds shared prompt_toolkit multiline input and opt-in reasoning presentation, with a chunk-boundary risk that can omit answer text from history.
